examples.en: Please turn right at the next traffic circle.

examples.ko: 로터리를 한 바퀴 돌고 나서야 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I only found the road after going around the traffic circle once.

examples.ko: 아침마다 로터리 앞에서 차가 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: Every morning the traffic backs up a lot in front of the traffic circle.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 시청 앞 로터리 근처예요.
examples.en: My house is near the traffic circle in front of City Hall.
There is a big fountain in the middle of the traffic circle.
Is the meeting place the cafe across from the traffic circle?

explain: '시청 앞 로터리'처럼 장소 이름 뒤에 붙여 길 이름처럼 부르기도 해요. 도로 안내에서는 '회전교차로'라는 말도 써요. '로터리를 돌다'처럼 움직임을 나타내는 말과 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: People often attach it to a place name, as in '시청 앞 로터리', and use it like a road name. In road guidance the term '회전교차로' is also used. It often pairs with movement verbs, as in '로터리를 돌다'.

en: wanting to go to the toilet; feeling an urge to urinate

examples.ko: 영화 보는 중에 갑자기 오줌이 마려워졌어요.
examples.en: In the middle of the movie I suddenly needed to pee.

examples.ko: 아이가 오줌이 마렵다고 해서 차를 세웠어요.
examples.en: The child said he needed to pee, so I pulled the car over.
I drank a lot of coffee, so I keep needing to go.
I really need to pee. Where is the restroom?

examples.ko: 긴 버스 안에서 갑자기 마려우면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What do you do if you suddenly need to go on a long bus ride?

examples.ko: 어제는 시험 보는 내내 마려워서 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I needed to go the whole time during the test, so it was hard.

explain: '오줌이 마렵다'처럼 꼭 '이/가'와 함께 써요. 어른이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 '화장실에 가고 싶어요'라고 돌려 말하는 경우가 많아요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '마려워요', '마려운', '마려우면'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is always used with '이/가', as in '오줌이 마렵다'. With adults or people you just met, people often say '화장실에 가고 싶어요' instead to be more indirect. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '마려워요', '마려운' and '마려우면'.

examples.en: Please draw a rhombus on the board.
This shape is not a square but a rhombus.
A baseball infield is shaped like a diamond.
I folded the paper and cut it into a diamond shape.
How are a rhombus and a square different?

examples.ko: 아이가 마름모 무늬 옷을 입고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is wearing clothes with a diamond pattern.

explain: 수학 시간에 '정사각형', '직사각형', '사다리꼴'과 함께 도형 이름으로 배워요. 일상에서는 '다이아몬드 모양'이라고도 말해요. 모양을 말할 때는 '마름모꼴'도 써요.
explain_en: You learn it in math class together with '정사각형', '직사각형' and '사다리꼴' as a shape name. In daily life people also say '다이아몬드 모양'. For the shape itself you can also say '마름모꼴'.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁은 마카로니 치즈를 만들 거예요.
examples.en: Tonight I'm going to make macaroni and cheese.

examples.ko: 마카로니를 삶을 때 소금을 조금 넣어요.
examples.en: When I boil macaroni, I add a little salt.
There is macaroni in the salad, so it's tasty.
The kids like macaroni soup.

examples.ko: 마카로니는 몇 분 정도 삶아야 해요?
examples.en: About how many minutes do I need to boil the macaroni?
I bought a bag of macaroni at the supermarket.

explain: 스파게티, 펜네처럼 파스타의 한 종류예요. 보통 '마카로니 샐러드', '마카로니 치즈'처럼 다른 음식 이름과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is one kind of pasta, like spaghetti or penne. It is usually used together with other dish names, as in '마카로니 샐러드' or '마카로니 치즈'.

examples.en: In summer, cool makguksu is the best.

examples.ko: 춘천에 가면 막국수를 꼭 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: If you go to Chuncheon, be sure to try makguksu.
Please add vinegar and mustard to your makguksu.
This place's makguksu comes in a big portion.
Not the spicy mixed one, please give me the cold broth makguksu.
Do you want to go eat makguksu for lunch today?

explain: 메밀로 만든 국수라서 '메밀국수'와 가까운 음식이에요. 하지만 막국수는 강원도 쪽 음식 이름으로 알려져 있어요. 식당에서는 국물이 있는 '물 막국수'와 양념에 비비는 '비빔 막국수'로 나눠 주문해요.
explain_en: It is a buckwheat noodle dish, so it is close to '메밀국수'. But makguksu is known as a food associated with the Gangwon region. At restaurants you order either '물 막국수' with broth or '비빔 막국수' mixed with sauce.

examples.en: The youngest daughter looks the most like her father.

examples.ko: 막내딸 덕분에 우리 집은 늘 웃음이 끊이지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to our youngest daughter, our house is always full of laughter.
Our youngest daughter became a college student this year.
I sent a little pocket money to my youngest daughter.
I went to the market with my youngest daughter.
I prepared a birthday cake for my youngest daughter.

explain: 딸 중에서 가장 어린 딸이에요. 반대로 첫째 딸은 '맏딸'이라고 해요. 집에서 부를 때는 이름 대신 '막내야'라고 부르는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It means the youngest of the daughters. The opposite, the eldest daughter, is '맏딸'. At home people often call her '막내야' instead of using her name.

examples.en: On April Fool's Day, my friend lied to me.
Tomorrow is April 1st, April Fool's Day.
Since it was April Fool's Day, I sent a text as a joke.
I was completely fooled by my friend's April Fool's lie.
What are you going to do this April Fool's Day?

examples.ko: 만우절 때 선생님이 농담을 하셔서 다 같이 웃었어요.
examples.en: On April Fool's Day our teacher made a joke, and we all laughed together.

explain: '만우절 거짓말', '만우절 장난'처럼 짝을 이뤄 자주 써요. 4월 1일이지만 쉬는 날은 아니에요. 가볍게 장난치는 날이라서 심한 거짓말은 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It pairs with words as in '만우절 거짓말' and '만우절 장난'. It falls on April 1st, but it is not a day off. It is a day for light pranks, so it's better not to tell serious lies.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 만화가가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to become a cartoonist since I was little.

examples.ko: 이 웹툰 만화가는 매주 새 이야기를 올려요.
examples.en: This webtoon cartoonist posts a new story every week.
I got an autograph from the cartoonist.
I saw a popular cartoonist's studio on TV.
They say making a living as a cartoonist isn't easy.

examples.ko: 동생은 만화가를 꿈꾸며 매일 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling dreams of being a cartoonist and draws every day.

explain: '-가'는 화가, 음악가, 소설가처럼 그 일을 직업으로 하는 사람 뒤에 붙어요. 웹툰을 그리는 사람은 '웹툰 작가'라고도 불러요. '만화가 재미있다'의 '만화+가(조사)'와 모양이 같으니 문장 속에서 구별해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-가' attaches to people who do something as a profession, as in 화가, 음악가 and 소설가. Someone who draws webtoons is also called a '웹툰 작가'. It looks the same as '만화+가' (subject particle) in '만화가 재미있다', so tell them apart from context.

examples.en: My mother is the eldest son's wife, so she is busy every holiday.
She says she learned a lot of housework after marrying in as the eldest son's wife.
On holidays the eldest son's wife prepares the ritual food.
My sister-in-law is the eldest son's wife.
She said the role of the eldest son's wife is not easy.
My aunt, who is the eldest son's wife, always looks after the family.

explain: '맏-'은 맏아들, 맏딸, 맏형처럼 '첫째'를 나타내요. 맏며느리는 첫째 아들의 아내를 말해요. 발음은 [만며느리]로, 'ㄷ'이 'ㄴ'처럼 소리 나요.
explain_en: The prefix '맏-' means 'eldest', as in 맏아들, 맏딸 and 맏형. 맏며느리 is the wife of the eldest son. It is pronounced [만며느리], with ㄷ sounding like ㄴ.

examples.en: You must not talk back to your parents.
I'm worried because my child keeps talking back.
Talking back to an adult is not polite.
Stop talking back and do your homework first.
He's in puberty these days, so he talks back more.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 지적을 받으면 꼭 말대답부터 해요.
examples.en: That friend always talks back first whenever he is corrected.

explain: 윗사람이 한 말에 반박하듯 대꾸하는 것을 말해서 대개 부정적인 느낌이에요. 그냥 질문에 답하는 것은 '대답'이라고 하고, '말대답'은 보통 '하다'와 함께 써요. '말대꾸'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It means answering back as if arguing with something an elder or superior said, so it usually has a negative feel. Simply answering a question is '대답', while '말대답' normally goes with '하다'. '말대꾸' is used with a similar meaning.

examples.en: In a cave, voices echo loudly.

examples.ko: 녹음 파일의 음질이 나빠서 말소리를 알아듣기 어려워요.
examples.en: The recording quality is bad, so it's hard to make out the speech.
The baby reacts to her mother's voice and smiles.

examples.ko: 시끄러워서 친구의 말소리도 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: It's so noisy that I can't even hear my friend's voice well.

examples.ko: 옆집 말소리 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of the voices from next door.
Please keep your voices down in the library.

explain: '목소리'는 그 사람만의 소리(목소리가 좋다)이고, '말소리'는 말하면서 나는 소리 자체를 가리켜요. 그래서 '말소리가 들리다', '말소리를 낮추다'처럼 들리는 소리나 크기를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 발음은 [말쏘리]예요.
explain_en: '목소리' is a person's own voice (as in '목소리가 좋다'), while '말소리' refers to the sound of speech itself. So it fits when talking about audibility or volume, as in '말소리가 들리다' and '말소리를 낮추다'. It is pronounced [말쏘리].

examples.ko: 맘씨가 착한 사람과 친구가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be friends with a kind-hearted person.
She is known as a good-natured neighbor.

examples.ko: 맘씨 고운 할머니가 떡을 나눠 주셨어요.
examples.en: A sweet-hearted grandmother shared rice cakes with us.
Her face is pretty, but her heart is even prettier.
He's a friend with a really good heart, at least.

examples.ko: 맘씨 나쁜 사람은 아니니까 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: He isn't a mean person, so don't worry.

explain: '마음씨'를 줄여서 말하는 형태로, 대화에서 편하게 써요. '착하다, 곱다, 좋다, 나쁘다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 나와요. 사람이 마음을 쓰는 모습을 말할 때 쓰고, 기분이나 감정을 말할 때는 '기분', '마음'을 써요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '마음씨' and is easy to use in conversation. It often pairs with words such as 착하다, 곱다, 좋다 and 나쁘다. It describes how kind a person is at heart; for mood or feelings you use '기분' or '마음'.

examples.en: My younger sibling broke my laptop.

examples.ko: 공공시설을 망가뜨리면 벌금을 내야 할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you damage public facilities, you may have to pay a fine.
Be careful not to break the toy by mistake.
I didn't break it on purpose.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 우산을 또 망가뜨려서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because my child broke the new umbrella again.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 먹는 야식이 다이어트를 완전히 망가뜨려요.
examples.en: Late-night snacks completely ruin a diet.

explain: 물건이 저절로 고장 나면 '망가지다', 누군가 그렇게 만들면 '망가뜨리다'를 써요. '망가트리다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓸 수 있어요. 물건뿐 아니라 계획, 기분, 건강처럼 보이지 않는 것을 엉망으로 만들 때도 써요.
explain_en: When something breaks by itself you use '망가지다', and when someone causes it you use '망가뜨리다'. '망가트리다' can be used with the same meaning. It works not only for objects but also for things like plans, mood and health that get ruined.

examples.en: I'll pour you some hot tea in a mug.
My friend gave me a mug as a birthday present.
Can I put this mug in the microwave?

examples.ko: 회사 책상 위에 머그잔이 세 개나 있어요.
examples.en: There are three mugs on my desk at work.
Could you wash just one mug for me?

examples.ko: 손잡이가 달린 머그잔이라서 뜨거워도 들기 편해요.
examples.en: It's a mug with a handle, so it's easy to hold even when hot.

explain: '컵'은 더 넓게 쓰는 말이고, '머그잔'은 손잡이가 달린 큼직한 잔을 말해요. '머그컵'이라고도 해요. 마시는 것에 따라 '찻잔', '커피잔'처럼도 부르고, 잔을 세는 말은 '개'를 써요.
explain_en: '컵' is the broader word, while '머그잔' is a large cup with a handle. People also say '머그컵'. Depending on what you drink you may also say '찻잔' or '커피잔', and you count cups with '개'.

examples.en: I was furious, but I held it in.
I got soaked in the rain from head to toe.

examples.ko: 키가 커서 머리끝이 천장에 닿을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm so tall that the top of my head almost touches the ceiling.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 머리끝이 쭈뼛 섰어요.
examples.en: Hearing that made the hair on my head stand on end.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 머리끝에서 발끝까지 흰옷을 입고 있었어요.
examples.en: That person was dressed in white from head to toe.
The child pulled the blanket over his head and hid.

explain: '머리끝부터 발끝까지'처럼 '발끝'과 짝으로 써서 온몸을 말해요. 머리 위 한가운데를 정확히 가리킬 때는 '정수리'라고 해요. 화가 크게 났을 때 쓰는 표현도 있어요.

phrases.example: 동생이 약속을 어겨서 머리끝까지 화가 났어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참기 어려울 만큼 몹시 화가 날 때 써요. 실제로 머리에서 화가 난다는 뜻이 아니라 화가 가득 찼다는 과장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so angry you can hardly hold it in. It is an exaggeration meaning anger fills you up, not about the head itself.

phrases.example: 무서운 이야기를 듣고 머리끝이 쭈뼛 섰어요.
phrases.en: I heard a scary story and my hair stood on end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 몹시 무섭거나 놀랐을 때 써요. 실제로 머리카락이 서는 것이 아니라 소름이 돋을 만큼 겁이 났다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are suddenly very scared or startled. It means you got chills of fear, not that your hair literally stands up.
phrases.en_equiv: make your hair stand on end

explain_en: It pairs with '발끝' in '머리끝부터 발끝까지' to mean the whole body. To point exactly to the crown of the head, you say '정수리'. There is also an expression that uses it for being very angry.

examples.en: I held my bangs in place with a small hairpin.
I bought a pretty hairpin at a gift shop.
My hairpin keeps falling out, so it's annoying.
I pinned my bangs up with two hairpins.
How much is that red hairpin over there?
Please wrap the hairpin I'm giving to my younger sibling.

explain: 머리핀은 보통 '꽂다'를 쓰고, 끈으로 묶는 '머리끈'은 '묶다'를 써서 동사가 달라요. 머리에 하는 것은 '머리핀을 꽂다', '머리띠를 하다'처럼 말해요. 영어식으로 '헤어핀'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: For a hairpin you usually use the verb '꽂다', while for a hair tie '머리끈' you use '묶다', so the verbs differ. Things worn in the hair go with different verbs, as in '머리핀을 꽂다' and '머리띠를 하다'. It is also called '헤어핀', the English-style word.

examples.ko: 시장에 가면 먹을거리 구경하는 재미가 있어요.
examples.en: Going to the market is fun for looking at all the food.

examples.ko: 소풍 갈 때 먹을거리를 넉넉히 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed plenty of food for the picnic.
Seoul has plenty of both sights and food.
Food booths are lined up at the festival.

examples.ko: 먹을거리는 제가 준비할 테니 음료만 사 오세요.
examples.en: I'll prepare the food, so just bring drinks.
These days people care a lot about safe food.

explain: '음식'보다 '먹을 수 있는 것들'이라는 느낌이 강해서 시장, 축제, 여행 이야기에 잘 어울려요. '먹거리'도 표준어로 같이 써요. '볼거리', '즐길 거리'와 짝을 이뤄 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It feels more like 'things to eat' than '음식', so it suits talk about markets, festivals and trips. '먹거리' is also a standard word with the same meaning. It often appears in a set with '볼거리' and '즐길 거리'.

examples.en: Far out at sea the wind blows very hard.
Fishing boats go out to the open sea and catch fish.
They say the waves far out at sea are very high today.

examples.ko: 먼바다 날씨가 나빠서 배가 못 떠요.
examples.en: The weather out at sea is bad, so the boats can't leave.
The anglers took a boat out to the open sea.

examples.ko: 먼바다에서 큰 배가 천천히 다가오고 있어요.
examples.en: A big ship is slowly approaching from far out at sea.

explain: 일기예보에서 육지에서 가까운 '앞바다'와 짝으로 나와요. '먼 바다'처럼 띄지 않고 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '먼바다로 나가다'처럼 방향을 나타내는 조사와 자주 써요.
explain_en: In weather forecasts it appears as the pair of '앞바다', the sea close to land. It is written as one word, not spaced like '먼 바다'. It is often used with direction particles, as in '먼바다로 나가다'.

examples.ko: 황사 때문에 방금 세차한 차가 금방 먼지투성이가 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the yellow dust, my freshly washed car quickly got covered in dust.
The room that has been empty for a long time is covered in dust.
I wiped the dusty bookshelf clean.
The child came home covered in dust.
The storeroom is dusty all over, so it needs cleaning.
Don't touch your face with dusty hands.

explain: '-투성이'는 흙투성이, 땀투성이, 상처투성이처럼 안 좋은 것이 온통 묻거나 가득할 때 붙여요. 보통 좋은 뜻의 말에는 쓰지 않아요. '먼지투성이가 되다', '먼지투성이다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The suffix '-투성이' attaches to something unpleasant that covers or fills a thing, as in 흙투성이, 땀투성이 and 상처투성이. It is not normally used with positive things. You use it as in '먼지투성이가 되다' and '먼지투성이다'.

examples.en: I decided to enter the long jump at the sports day.
In the long jump, the run-up is very important.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 멀리뛰기를 잘해서 상도 받았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is good at the long jump and even won a prize.
We measured our long jump results in PE class.
A long jumper lands in the sand pit.
The long jump is easier than the high jump.

explain: 짝이 되는 종목은 '높이뛰기'예요. 학교 체력 검사에서는 제자리에서 뛰는 '제자리멀리뛰기'도 해요. 경기를 '하다', 기록을 '재다'와 자주 써요.
explain_en: The paired event is '높이뛰기' (high jump). In school fitness tests there is also '제자리멀리뛰기', a standing long jump. It often goes with '하다' for doing the event and '재다' for measuring the result.

examples.en: The puppy stands far away and looks at me.
I stepped well back to take a picture.

examples.ko: 불꽃놀이는 멀찍이 앉아서 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to watch fireworks from a seat some distance away.
He stepped far back and watched us.
I parked the car some distance away and walked.
The children threw the ball from a good distance away.

explain: '멀리'보다 '꽤 멀게 떨어져서'라는 느낌이고, 일부러 거리를 둔 것처럼 들릴 때가 많아요. '떨어지다, 서다, 물러나다, 앉다' 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. '멀찌감치'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '멀리', it gives the feel of 'at a fair distance', and often sounds like keeping distance on purpose. It fits verbs such as 떨어지다, 서다, 물러나다 and 앉다. '멀찌감치' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: This outfit looks too dull.

examples.ko: 멋없는 발표라서 아무도 박수를 안 쳤어요.
examples.en: It was such a dull presentation that nobody clapped.
I'm really sorry for saying it so tactlessly.
The movie's ending was lame, so I was disappointed.
Please don't think the present is boring.
So what if it's not stylish? It's fine as long as it's comfortable.

explain: 반대말은 '멋있다'예요. '재미없다'는 흥미가 없다는 뜻이고, '멋없다'는 세련되지 않았거나 분위기가 없다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있으니 조심해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '멋있다'. '재미없다' means not interesting, while '멋없다' suggests unstylish or lacking charm. Saying it directly to a person can sound rude, so be careful.

examples.en: An Olympic medalist came to our school to give a talk.
That athlete is a medalist at a world championship.
The three medalists stepped onto the podium.

examples.ko: 저는 메달리스트를 꿈꾸며 매일 새벽에 훈련해요.
examples.en: I train every dawn, dreaming of becoming a medalist.
I saw a medalist's interview on the news yesterday.
There is prize money for the medalists of this competition.

explain: '금메달리스트', '은메달리스트', '동메달리스트'처럼 앞에 색을 붙여 써요. 메달을 땄다는 말은 '메달을 따다'라고 해요. 뉴스와 스포츠 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You can put the color in front, as in '금메달리스트', '은메달리스트' and '동메달리스트'. Winning a medal is said '메달을 따다'. It often appears in news and sports talk.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 차가운 메밀국수가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On hot days I want to eat cold buckwheat noodles.
I tried eating the buckwheat noodles with grated radish.
Buckwheat noodles are a bit coarse and nutty.
I ordered a bowl of buckwheat noodles for lunch.
After boiling the buckwheat noodles, rinse them in cold water.
This restaurant is famous for its buckwheat noodles.

explain: '막국수'도 메밀로 만든 국수라서 서로 가까운 음식이에요. 일본어 '소바'를 한국어로는 '메밀국수'라고 옮기는 경우가 많아요. 국수는 '삶다', 찬물에 '헹구다'처럼 요리 동사와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: '막국수' is also made from buckwheat, so the two dishes are close. The Japanese 'soba' is often rendered in Korean as '메밀국수'. It appears with cooking verbs such as '삶다' (boil) and '헹구다' (rinse).

examples.en: The melodrama I watched yesterday was really sad.
I like melodramas more than action.
The lead of this melodrama is a famous actor.
Melodramas usually feature love stories.

examples.ko: 멜로드라마 속 장면 같은 일이 생겼어요!
examples.en: Something like a scene from a melodrama happened!
My parents watch melodramas too on weekends.

explain: 줄여서 '멜로'라고도 해요. 사랑과 이별을 다룬 드라마나 영화를 가리켜요. 웃음이 중심인 '로맨틱 코미디'와는 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It is often shortened to '멜로'. It refers to dramas and films about love and parting. People distinguish it from a 'romantic comedy', which centers on laughs.

examples.en: The mother dressed the child in overalls.

examples.ko: 멜빵바지는 어깨끈 길이를 조절할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With overalls you can adjust the length of the shoulder straps.
Denim overalls really suit you.
Overalls with a white T-shirt look cute.
My younger sibling came out wearing overalls.
I ordered a pair of overalls online.

explain: '멜빵'만 말하면 어깨에 걸어 바지를 고정하는 끈이에요. 그 끈이 달린 바지가 '멜빵바지'예요. 바지이므로 동사는 '입다'를 쓰고, 한 벌, 두 벌로 세요.
explain_en: '멜빵' alone means the straps that hang from the shoulders to hold up trousers. Trousers with those straps are '멜빵바지'. As trousers, the verb is '입다', and you count them as 한 벌, 두 벌.

examples.en: In summer you have to get mosquito spray first.
I sprayed mosquito repellent in the room, and the mosquitoes disappeared.
I bought mosquito spray to get rid of mosquitoes at home.
The smell of the mosquito spray is too strong.

examples.ko: 모기약이 다 떨어져서 하나 사 와야 해요.
examples.en: The mosquito spray ran out, so I have to buy one.
Mosquito repellent is a must when you go camping.

explain: 모기를 쫓거나 없애는 약을 두루 가리켜서 뿌리는 것도, 피부에 바르는 것도 '모기약'이라고 말해요. 방 안에서 태우는 것은 '모기향'이라고 해요. 동사는 '뿌리다'나 '바르다'를 써요.
explain_en: It covers medicines that repel or kill mosquitoes in general, so both sprays and skin-applied products can be called '모기약'. What you burn in a room is called '모기향'. The verbs are '뿌리다' (spray) or '바르다' (apply).

examples.en: I lit a mosquito coil in the yard.
The smell of the mosquito coil spread through the room.
You really need a mosquito coil at a campsite.

examples.ko: 마트에 간 김에 모기향도 하나 사 왔어요.
examples.en: Since I was at the mart, I bought a mosquito coil too.
My throat stings because of the mosquito coil smoke.

examples.ko: 모기향 피운 뒤에는 꼭 환기를 해 주세요.
examples.en: After burning a mosquito coil, please be sure to air out the room.

explain: 불을 붙여 연기를 내는 모기향은 '피우다'와 함께 써요. 뿌리거나 바르는 '모기약'과는 쓰는 방법이 달라요. 연기가 나므로 사용한 뒤에는 환기하라는 말을 자주 해요.
explain_en: Mosquito incense, which you light to make smoke, goes with the verb '피우다'. It is used differently from '모기약', which you spray or apply. Since it makes smoke, people often remind you to air out the room afterward.

examples.en: The children are building a sand castle on the beach.
A wave came and the sand castle collapsed.
Shall we build a sand castle together?

examples.ko: 기초가 약한 계획은 모래성처럼 금방 무너져요.
examples.en: A plan with a weak foundation collapses quickly like a sand castle.
I stuck a small flag on top of the sand castle.

examples.ko: 모래성에 물을 조금 부으면 더 단단해져요.
examples.en: If you pour a little water on the sand castle, it gets firmer.

explain: 모래성은 '쌓다, 만들다'와 함께 쓰고, 무너질 때는 '무너지다', 일부러 부술 때는 '허물다'를 써요. 기초가 약해서 쉽게 무너질 것을 비유할 때도 '모래성'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use '쌓다' or '만들다' for building one, '무너지다' when it collapses, and '허물다' when you tear it down on purpose. '모래성' is also used figuratively for something so poorly founded that it falls apart easily.

examples.en: Sand got into my shoe, so it's uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 모래알처럼 많은 별이 하늘에 떠 있었어요.
examples.en: Stars as countless as grains of sand filled the sky.
Each grain of sand sparkled in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 손으로 모래알을 한 줌 쥐어 봤어요.
examples.en: I scooped up a handful of sand grains.
I walked barefoot, and the sand grains stung my soles.
A bug as small as a grain of sand landed on my arm.

explain: 모래 한 알 한 알을 가리켜서 아주 작고 많은 것을 비유할 때 써요. '밥이 모래알 같다'는 말처럼 맛이 없을 때도 비유로 써요. 한 알은 '모래 한 알'이라고 하고, 모래 전체는 그냥 '모래'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 감기에 걸려서 밥이 모래알을 씹는 것 같아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입맛이 없거나 기분이 안 좋아서 음식이 아무 맛도 안 날 때 써요. 실제로 모래가 들어 있다는 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have no appetite or feel low and food has no taste. It does not mean there is real sand in it.

explain_en: It points to individual grains of sand, so it is used to compare things that are tiny and numerous. It is also used figuratively when food is tasteless, as in '밥이 모래알 같다'. One grain is '모래 한 알', while sand in general is just '모래'.

examples.en: I caught a throat cold and my voice won't come out.
My throat cold was bad, so I went to the doctor.

examples.ko: 목감기 걸렸을 때는 따뜻한 물을 마셔요.
examples.en: When I have a throat cold, I drink warm water.
A throat cold should get better after a few days of rest.

examples.ko: 아이가 목감기 때문에 밥을 잘 못 먹어요.
examples.en: My child can't eat well because of a throat cold.
Every winter I'm never free of a throat cold.

explain: 목이 붓고 아프면서 기침이 나는 감기를 말해요. '코감기', '몸살감기'와 증상에 따라 나눠 불러요. '목감기에 걸리다'라고 하고, 다른 사람에게 옮을 때는 '감기가 옮다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a cold with a swollen, painful throat and coughing. People distinguish it from '코감기' and '몸살감기' by symptoms. You say '목감기에 걸리다', and when it passes from someone else you say '감기가 옮다'.

examples.en: When class ended, the students poured out through the school gate.
After the show ends, the audience pours out all at once.
They say people are pouring out into the streets to see the fireworks.

examples.ko: 지하철 문이 열리자 사람들이 몰려나오기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the subway doors opened, people began to pour out.
The sight of children rushing out to the playground is cute.
Fans will pour out when the game ends, so let's hurry.

explain: 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 나올 때 쓰고, 한 사람이 나올 때는 쓰지 않아요. 반대로 안으로 들어올 때는 '몰려들다', 이쪽으로 올 때는 '몰려오다'를 써요. '학생들이', '관객들이'처럼 여러 명을 나타내는 주어와 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when many people come out at once, not for a single person. For crowds going inside you use '몰려들다', and for coming toward you '몰려오다'. It often takes plural subjects such as '학생들이' or '관객들이'.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 몸동작을 크게 하면 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: If you make big body movements during a presentation, you stand out.
We couldn't communicate in words, so I explained with gestures.
The child's movements are very cute.
In dance class, every single movement matters.

examples.ko: 나라마다 몸동작의 뜻이 다를 수 있어요.
examples.en: The meaning of a gesture can differ from country to country.

examples.ko: 강아지의 몸동작을 보면 기분을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell a dog's mood by its body movements.

explain: '몸짓'과 뜻이 가까워요. 손만 움직일 때는 '손짓'이라고 해요. 운동이나 춤에서 몸을 움직이는 방법을 말할 때도 쓰고, '크게 하다', '따라 하다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is close in meaning to '몸짓'. When only the hands move, you say '손짓'. It is also used for how the body moves in exercise or dance, and it goes well with '크게 하다' and '따라 하다'.

en: cold with body aches; flu-like cold

examples.ko: 몸살감기에 걸려서 하루 종일 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I caught a flu-like cold and lay down all day.
My whole body aches, as if a flu-like cold is coming.
For a flu-like cold, getting plenty of rest is best.
I took a day off work because of a flu-like cold.
I took cold-and-body-ache medicine and went to bed early.

examples.ko: 열이 나고 으슬으슬한 걸 보니 몸살감기 같아요.
examples.en: With a fever and chills, it seems like a flu-like cold.

explain: 감기에 온몸이 쑤시고 열이 나는 몸살이 함께 온 상태를 말해요. '몸살'만 말해도 비슷하게 통해요. '감기에 걸리다'와 달리 몸살은 '몸살이 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a cold that comes together with aching all over and a fever. Saying just '몸살' is understood in a similar way. Unlike a cold, which you '걸리다', body aches can also be '몸살이 나다'.

examples.en: I learned how to greet people in Mongolian from a Mongolian friend.
They say Mongolian has a word order similar to Korean.
I'm majoring in Mongolian at university.

examples.ko: 몽골어 수업이 일주일에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: There are Mongolian classes twice a week.
I'd like to try studying Mongolian later too.
A Mongolian interpreter attended the meeting.

explain: '몽골'에 '-어'를 붙여 언어 이름을 만들어요. 일본어, 영어, 러시아어처럼 나라 이름에 '-어'가 붙는 말이 많아요. '몽골어를 배우다', '몽골어로 말하다'처럼 '을/를'과 '(으)로'를 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: Adding '-어' to '몽골' gives the name of the language, like 일본어, 영어 and 러시아어. Use '을/를' for the object and '(으)로' for the language used, as in '몽골어를 배우다' and '몽골어로 말하다'.

examples.en: There are many young people who are indifferent to politics.

examples.ko: 주민들이 쓰레기 문제에 무관심해서 동네가 지저분해졌어요.
examples.en: The residents are indifferent to the garbage problem, so the neighborhood got dirty.
My husband is too indifferent to housework.
You must not treat a child with indifference.

examples.ko: 저는 유행에는 무관심하니까 신경 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: I don't care about trends, so please don't worry about me.

examples.ko: 남들이 뭐라 해도 그는 무관심할 뿐이에요.
examples.en: No matter what others say, he just doesn't care.

explain: '정치에 무관심하다'처럼 대상 뒤에 '에'를 붙여요. 반대는 '관심이 많다', '관심이 있다'예요. 사람에게 쓰면 비난하는 느낌이 있어서 윗사람에게 직접 말할 때는 조심해요.
explain_en: Attach '에' to the thing you are indifferent to, as in '정치에 무관심하다'. The opposite is '관심이 많다' or '관심이 있다'. Used about a person it carries a tone of criticism, so be careful saying it directly to someone senior.

examples.en: Children aged 6 and under get free admission.
On Sundays the museum has free admission, so it's crowded.

examples.ko: 학생증을 보여 주면 무료입장을 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you show your student ID, you can get in for free.
By any chance, is today's event free to enter?
Free admission starts at five in the afternoon.
The poster said 'free admission', so I went in.

explain: 안내문과 광고에서 많이 보는 말이고, '입장 무료'라고도 써요. 말로 할 때는 '무료로 들어가다'나 '공짜로 들어가다'도 써요. 반대는 돈을 내고 들어가는 '유료'예요.
explain_en: It is common on notices and ads and is also written '입장 무료'. In speech you can say '무료로 들어가다' or the casual '공짜로 들어가다'. The opposite is '유료', where you pay to enter.

examples.ko: 약속을 해 놓고 연락도 없이 안 오다니, 정말 무책임해요.
examples.en: Making a promise and not showing up without a word is really irresponsible.

examples.ko: 담당자가 무책임한 탓에 문제가 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: The problem got bigger because the person in charge was irresponsible.
Don't talk irresponsibly; take responsibility to the end.

examples.ko: 그 사장님은 직원들에게 무책임하다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: That boss was told by his staff that he was irresponsible.
If you take on a job and just leave, that's irresponsible.

examples.ko: 제가 무책임했던 것 같아요. 정말 죄송해요.
examples.en: I think I was irresponsible. I'm really sorry.

explain: 반대는 '책임감이 있다', '책임감이 강하다'예요. 명사 '무책임'은 '무책임 그 자체'처럼 쓰기도 해요. 상대를 강하게 비난하는 말이라서 직접 말할 때는 조심해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '책임감이 있다' or '책임감이 강하다'. The noun '무책임' can be used as in '무책임 그 자체' (irresponsibility itself). It strongly criticizes the other person, so be careful using it directly.
